p: brethren: Seeing that I have promised you deliverance, it remains that you encourage one another to embrace this promise, considering that you are my people on whom I will have mercy.
mother: God shows that the fault was not in him, that he forsook them, but in their Synagogue, and their idolatries; Isa 50:1.
from between her breasts: Meaning that their idolatry was so great, that they were not ashamed, but boasted of it; Eze 16:25.

set her as in the day: For even though his people were as a harlot for their idolatries, yet he had left them with their dress and dowry and certain signs of his favour, but if they continued still, he would utterly destroy them.
born: When I brought her out of Egypt. See Geneva "Eze 16:4"
children of whoredoms: That is bastards, and begotten in adultery.
lovers: Meaning the idol which they served, and by whom they thought they had wealth and abundance.
thy way with thorns: I will punish you so that you may then test whether your idols can help you, and bring you into such straightness that you will have no lust to play the harlot.
I will go and return to: This he speaks of the faithful, who are truly converted, and also shows the use and profit of God's punishments.
gave her corn: This declares that idolaters defraud God of his honour, when they attribute his benefits to their idols.
my corn in the time thereof: Signifying that God will take away his benefits, when man by his ingratitude abuses them.
lewdness in the sight of her: That is, all her service, ceremonies, and inventions by which she worshipped her idols.
Baalim: I will punish her for her idolatry.
earrings and her jewels: By showing how harlots trim themselves to please others, he declares how superstitious idolaters set a great part of their religion in adorning themselves on their holy days.
allure her: By my benefits in offering her grace and mercy, even in that place where she will think herself destitute of all help and comfort.

of Achor for a door of: Which was a plentiful valley, and in which they had great comfort when they came out of the wilderness, as in Jos 7:26, and is called the door of hope, because it was a departing from death and an entry into life.
sing there: She will then praise God as she did when she was delivered out of Egypt.
Ishi: That is, my husband, knowing that I am united to you by a covenant which could not be violated.
Baali: That is, my master: which name was applied to their idols.
name: No idolatry will come into their mouth at all, but they will fear me purely according to my word.
beasts of the field: Meaning that he will so bless them that all creatures will favour them.
faithfulness: With a covenant that will never be broken.
the heavens: Then will the heaven desire rain for the earth, which will bring forth things for the use of man.
